title: Protesters march to Mendiola as Trump visits Malacañang
summary: Protesters marched from Morayta heading to Mendiola in Manila as United States President Donald Trump visited Malacañang on Wednesday.

blocks.text: Protesters marched from Morayta heading to Mendiola in Manila as United States President Donald Trump visited Malacañang on Wednesday.
They are protesting the visit of Trump to attend the ASEAN Summit 2026 as well as the Pax Silica initiative, among others.

Thousands of protesters marched to Mendiola as United States President Donald Trump visited Malacañang on Wednesday morning. @gmanews https://t.co/W7u391xa4E— Joviland Rita (@jovilandxrita) November 18, 2026
The protesters marching along Recto Avenue stopped at a police barricade at San Sebastian Street, where they held a program. Around 11 a.m., the protesters were seen running along Recto Avenue.
BAYAN secretary general Raymond Palatino told GMA News Online that more than 2,000 people joined the “Trump Out” rally despite what he described as police restrictions and sabotage operations.
Palatino described the protest as successful.
“Successful 'yung Trump Out protest despite the restrictions, sabotage operations of the police,” he said.
“We condemned the barrier, the overkill security measures. We condemn the use of public money for container vans, barbed wire to suppress free speech,” he added.
Protesters also burned a US flag when Trump arrived at Malacañang.
“When Trump arrived in Malacañang, we burned the US flag, and then there was protest in the street. That's important. Kasi red carpet welcome ni Marcos pero tayo protest,” Palatino said.
He said the protest sought to hold Trump accountable for what he described as a war of aggression. He also cited rising oil prices as one of the concerns of protesters.
He added Trump's agenda during his visit to the Philippines was not for the benefit of Filipinos. —AOL, GMA News
